text:
ashley: FYI — CISO proposed reducing audit log sampling in eu-west to curb S3 egress and long-term retention costs. They mentioned cutting from 100% -> 10% for KMS/keystore events. This will be a policy request, but wanted a quick ops/security risk call. @tariq can you weigh in on operational impact?

tariq: Do we have numbers on what triggers get dropped? Is it all KMS decrypts or just high-cardinality headers?

ashley: It's across the pipeline (keystore RPCs, KMS decrypt traces, and VPC flowlog enrichments). Ballpark: ~2.4TB/day of additional exported logs for eu-west at current retention; sampling to 10% saves ~2TB/day. CISO cares about cost and vendor audit exposure.

kevin: Reducing sampling that aggressively is risky for EU regulatory customers. We would lose the signal to investigate cross-account grants and STS anomalies. Can we instead compress and shorten retention for non-critical buckets? :thinking:

ops-oncall: Operational note — when we tried a similar sampling test in staging last quarter we masked transient KMS decrypt errors. That led to delayed GPU node joins because keystore decrypt fallbacks failed silently. We'll need synthetic checks or alerts if sampling changes.

maria: Suggest a staged approach: (1) Canary eu-west-A with 50% sampling + synthetic KMS decrypt probes; (2) if stable 1w, drop to 25% for non-auth events; (3) keep 100% for auth/privileged change events. Also add an automated fallback to full-emit when error-rate for KMS decrypts > 0.5%.

ashley: agree. CISO wants quick ROI calc and rollback plan. Can we document a 2-week canary and guard rails? Also need a short note for compliance on why critical audit paths remain intact.

security-bot: Policy change ticket created: SEC-2026-347. Assigned: kevin (owner), ops-oncall (runbook), tariq (telemetry). Priority: P2. Link: https://redwood.internal/sec/ticket/SEC-2026-347

kevin: I'll own the compliance writeup. Ops — can you draft the rollback playbook? Minimal steps: toggle sampling flag, rehydrate exports if needed, notify compliance.

ops-oncall: Drafting runbook now. Quick CLI toggle for the feature flag (k8s configmap) — testing in staging first:

```
# set sampling to 0.5 (50%) for keystore events in eu-west canary
kubectl -n infra-telemetry patch configmap audit-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"eu-west.keystore.sampling":"0.5"}}'
```

ops-oncall: Also adding a synthetic probe: `curl -sS https://keystore-canary.eu-west/api/v1/decrypt -d '@test-payload'` and assert 200 + valid signature. If >3 failures in 5m, revert sampling to 1.0 and page oncall.

tariq: Telemetry ask: add a short-lived Prom rule for KMS error-rate and for 'keystore-decrypt-latency' p99. We'll trigger rollback automatically.

maria: +1 on automatic rollback. Also recommend we blacklist sampling for any events with user_token or cross_account flags — keep those 100%.

ashley: Good plan. Action items: kevin -> compliance note by EOD, ops-oncall -> runbook + CLI toggles by EOD, tariq -> prometheus rules and dashboards by tomorrow morning. I'll coordinate with CISO on canary timeline and cost numbers. :thumbsup:

kevin: One more idea — before sampling, try changing exporter to better compression (snappy) and dedupe pipeline; might buy us 30-40% without losing fidelity. I'll add to the writeup.

ashley: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after runbook + telemetry are in. If synthetic probes fail during canary, rollback immediately.

ops-oncall: Noted. I'll post the initial runbook draft to the ticket thread in 30m.

kevin: acked.

maria: tagging @compliance for visibility.

ashley: closing loop here — leaving SEC-2026-347 as the canonical thread.
